DOCUMENT:
"""
Large-scale image generation has benefited from advances in data scale, quality, rebalancing, and recaptioning, yet conventional pipelines typically optimize task-specific datasets in isolation. A central challenge is not only how to curate each task-specific corpus, but also how to organize heterogeneous supervision according to the dependencies among generative capabilities. 

To address this, we introduce a \textbf{capability-driven data infrastructure}, which refers to a data curation and training framework that explicitly structures data and supervision around distinct generative capabilities (such as text-to-image synthesis, image editing, and image-knowledge association). This infrastructure is guided by a \textbf{capability-aligned curriculum scheduling}, meaning that data and training are organized in stages that reflect the prerequisite relationships among these capabilities. For example, text-to-image grounding is treated as foundational, with editing and knowledge association building upon it.

Our infrastructure comprises three specialized yet interoperable data engines, each responsible for constructing supervision for a specific capability: (1) a text-image grounding engine, which pairs images with descriptive captions to support text-to-image generation; (2) an inter-image transformation engine, which creates editing pairs by associating source images with their edited counterparts and corresponding transformation instructions; and (3) an image-knowledge association engine, which links images to structured knowledge entities (such as objects or attributes) to enable knowledge-grounded generation. These engines operate in tandem, sharing data representations and enabling cross-task supervision.

To ensure consistency and quality across tasks, we employ \textbf{caption experts}, which are automated captioning models trained to generate high-quality, task-aligned descriptions. These models are used to harmonize supervision between text-to-image (T2I) and editing tasks, ensuring that captions and transformation instructions are consistent and appropriately granular for each task.

The data curation process follows a multi-stage curriculum. In the initial stage, the focus is on assembling high-quality T2I pairs with broad visual and conceptual coverage. Subsequent stages introduce more complex editing and knowledge association tasks, with data quality, visual-concept diversity, and image resolution progressively increased. Progression through stages is determined by capability dependencies (e.g., editing data is only constructed for images with reliable T2I grounding) and by quality metrics such as caption accuracy and image fidelity. Capability-aware evaluation informs the curriculum by identifying gaps in coverage and triggering targeted data retrieval, expert construction, or resampling.

At scale, our framework curates a 440M-image T2I corpus, 120M editing pairs, and over 27M image-entity pairs. Data is sourced from publicly available image repositories and filtered using automated quality checks, including image resolution thresholds, content safety filters, and caption quality scoring. Additional validation is performed through sampling and manual inspection to ensure dataset integrity.

We train multimodal diffusion models from scratch at two scales, with 3B and 6B parameters respectively. For evaluation, we conduct quantitative analysis on CPI-Bench, reporting metrics such as FID (Fréchet Inception Distance), CLIP score, and retrieval accuracy, and compare against established baselines including Stable Diffusion and Imagen. Qualitative evaluations are performed across diverse text-to-image and editing scenarios, with human raters assessing visual fidelity, relevance, and editing accuracy.

Experimental results demonstrate that our models achieve competitive FID and CLIP scores on CPI-Bench, outperforming baselines in both text-to-image and editing tasks. Qualitative analysis shows broad visual coverage, versatile rendering, and effective transfer across generative capabilities, substantiating the benefits of our capability-driven data infrastructure.
"""
